title: Introduce RAG step-factory playbook and lightweight e2e devkit
author: Anika Rao
description: Context and motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for a compact, production-adjacent RAG quickstart that (1) defines reusable step templates for common pipeline stages (query rewrite, candidate fetch, rerank, synthesis), (2) ships a tiny devkit for deterministic e2e runs and replayable telemetry, and (3) demonstrates a connector pattern (GraphQL) used in real products. This PR introduces the 'step-factory' playbook: a curated set of YAML step templates, a node-based devkit runner with a lightweight in-memory index/replay harness, and docs + smoke CI to make authoring and testing RAG flows straightforward. What this contains (high level): - playbooks/step-factory/README.md with conceptual overview and authoring patterns - playbooks/step-factory/templates/* (5 canonical step templates: rewrite, retrieve, rerank, synthesize, commit) - devkit/runner/index.ts: small runner that composes steps, exposes a CLI (rw-step run --playbook playbooks/step-factory/demo.yaml) - devkit/replay/probes.ts: deterministic replay harness and step-level assertion helpers - examples/graphql-connector/sample-connector.ts: example adapter showing connector->tool-call pattern and auth stub - docs/site/content/quickstarts/step-factory.md: full quickstart for docs site with config snippets and troubleshooting - tests/e2e/step-factory.spec.ts: end-to-end smoke with seeded index and step assertions - ci/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml: nightly smoke and PR run (fast mode) Implementation notes: - Step templates are small YAML fragments (no infra assumptions). They reference minimal tool contracts (input/outputs) so teams can adapt them to Dedicated/Private deploys. - The devkit runner intentionally avoids heavy deps; it supports local in-memory corpora and a simple HTTP-based mock connector for external tools. - Replay harness records step inputs/outputs and asserts invariants (token budget, latency upper bound, structured-output schemas). - Example GraphQL connector demonstrates incremental indexing and delta-sync semantics for demo data sets. Migration and compatibility: - Non-breaking: templates are additive and the runner is opt-in. - If teams adopt the runner, they may want to replace the in-memory index with their existing vector store; the README includes migration pointers. Checklist (what I did): - [x] Add playbook templates and demo playbook - [x] Implement lightweight devkit runner + replay probes - [x] Add example GraphQL connector and auth stub - [x] Docs quickstart page + local CLI usage - [x] E2E smoke tests and CI workflow - [x] Add linear links and release notes Drafting notes: Linear ENG-8642 contains the design doc and acceptance criteria. See demo recording link (internal docs) in the Linear ticket. This description is intentionally long to aid reviewers and release notes.

release_notes: - New quickstart: 'Step Factory' playbook with 5 canonical RAG templates (rewrite, retrieve, rerank, synthesize, commit). - Lightweight devkit for deterministic local e2e runs and replayable step probes. - GraphQL connector example showing incremental index sync and tool-call pattern. - CI smoke workflow to run quickstart in PRs. See docs/quickstarts/step-factory for usage and migration notes.
usage_snippet: To try locally: 1) git checkout feature/step-factory-playbook-e2e-devkit 2) cd devkit && npm install && npm run build 3) rw-step run --playbook ../playbooks/step-factory/demo.yaml --mode local --seeded-index 4) npm run test:e2e for the smoke harness. The README includes a troubleshooting section for common auth and port collisions.
notes_for_release_manager: Safe to ship as docs/quickstart. No infra changes. Recommend publishing the docs page in next docs deploy; mark as non-breaking. The CI smoke workflow is opt-in for nightly on the first week after release to collect early telemetry.
